A1.justification: Both PDFs describe COPE, with matching core methods, experiments and appendix material despite the changed title and expanded scope. The complete text, equations, tables and rendered figures support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original mathematical reasoning and code-generation experiments in Tables 1–5, with additional analyses and repeated-run results in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original math and coding results and adds model configurations, baseline comparisons, MT-Bench evaluations and ALFWorld experiments.

M1.justification: The three-stage planning, execution and escalation procedure remains intact. v2 adds perplexity-based candidate selection and escalation for open-ended generation and applies planning and voting at individual agent action steps. Renaming reasoner to executor and explicitly specifying goal versus guideline plans do not independently establish method changes.

E1.justification: v2 adds MT-Bench multi-turn open-ended generation and ALFWorld interactive household tasks, substantially extending task requirements beyond mathematical reasoning and code generation. MATH-500, AIME-2024 and MBPP with MBPP-ET evaluation remain.

E2.justification: Tables 3–5 add evaluated ABC and FrugalGPT comparisons alongside the existing Cascade and standalone-model baselines. This substantially expands comparison methods to three-model cascading and trained routing; v1 explicitly excluded FrugalGPT because it required supervision.

E3.justification: v2 adds Qwen-2.5-1.5B configurations on MATH-500 and MBPP, plus an additional model for ABC. New evaluation designs include GPT-4o pairwise judging with position swapping on MT-Bench and Qwen3-8B/GPT-4.1 action-level evaluation on 134 ALFWorld tasks, using success rate and total evaluation cost.

E4.justification: Sample-count, truncation and threshold studies and the qualitative examples are retained. The difficulty analysis is narrowed: v1 Table 3 includes GPT-4o, standalone large-model and Cascade breakdowns, whereas v2 Table 9 retains only the small-model baselines and GPT-4o-mini COPE. Its appendix placement does not make this a new analysis.

E5.justification: Five independent seeded runs and standard-deviation reporting remain, but uncertainty coverage contracts substantially. v1 Table 9 reports both GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini comparisons, including Cascade variants; v2 Table 12 retains only GPT-4o-mini Large and COPE. Uncertainty estimates disappear for comparisons still present in the main results.

E6.justification: v2 adds ABC, FrugalGPT and Qwen-1.5B result entries, MT-Bench outcomes of 36.9% wins versus 35.0% losses, and ALFWorld success rates of 44.8% versus 42.5%. Original headline math/code totals remain. Appendix costs change from 202 to 212, repeated-run means are revised, and several difficulty and uncertainty result entries disappear.

T1.justification: The consensus definition and latent-variable/Bayesian equations are unchanged. v1 Section 6 and its appendix mixture-of-experts interpretation are consolidated in v2 Appendix B, without new mathematical assumptions, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion broaden the claimed effectiveness of COPE to open-ended and agent tasks and strengthen its positioning as broadly applicable efficient collaboration. v1's explicit contribution claim that planning addresses autoregressive generation's lack of global foresight is dropped.

C2.justification: v2 removes v1's explicit caveats about domain-specific adaptation and additional multi-round latency. It adds interpretations of perplexity as an effective confidence signal and attributes FrugalGPT's difficulties to its scorer's limited capacity. The central explanation of planning-mediated collaboration remains.

D1.justification: v2 identifies supplementary material as the code source, adds DistilBERT and ABC implementation information, and revises model-license disclosures. It removes v1's explicit four-shot Cascade and single-large-model-call implementation note. Hardware, API snapshots, temperatures, batch sizes and math/code prompts remain largely unchanged.

R1.justification: The main related-work themes remain, but cost-aware positioning adds ABC and replaces the exclusion of supervised routing with a capacity-based critique of FrugalGPT. AutoMix discussion and some speculative-decoding references disappear; DistilBERT and ALFWorld references are added.

P1.justification: v2 extensively rewrites and reorganizes the narrative, changes the title and author list, and replaces reasoner/round terminology with executor/stage. Contribution bullets become a research-question presentation; theory and broader impact move to appendices, appendix analyses are reorganized, and ethics and reproducibility statements are added.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout. Main results tables are substantially restructured around model combinations and training status, new task tables are added, and difficulty and uncertainty displays are reduced and relocated. The framework diagram is revised and moved, and Figure 2's displayed solution is shortened.

improvement.justification: Additional model configurations, ABC/FrugalGPT comparisons and evaluations beyond math/code strengthen evidence for generality and competitive cost efficiency, addressing v1's narrow empirical scope. The net gain is limited by reduced uncertainty coverage, removal of the latency caveat and incomplete new-task settings. v2 also overstates lowest coding cost: Table 5 reports ABC at 1267 versus COPE at 1279 for EXAONE/GPT-4o.
